taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes the generic placement of American ranids is unsettled (Rana, Lithobates or other genera depending on the arrangement) and follows Nicholson (2025) in using Lithobates; older names are Rana sphenocephala / Rana utricularia.
fieldMarks: Green or brown with irregularly spaced, rounded dark spots on the back and a few on the sides.
A continuous, usually yellowish ridge runs along each side of the back.
Head is pointed; usually a light spot in the centre of the eardrum.
Hind toes are extensively webbed; adults reach about 13 cm snout-vent length.
Breeding call is a short chuckling or ratchet-like trill; breeding males have spherical vocal sacs at the angles of the jaw.
behavior: Males call from shallow or deep water, floating or submerged, sometimes from crayfish burrows.
Breeds usually March-June in the north of the range and in any month in the far south.
In summer may disperse from water into moist upland vegetation; migrates between breeding pools and adjacent terrestrial habitat; inactive in cold winter weather in the north.
Adults eat small terrestrial invertebrates; egg masses are baseball-sized and hold roughly 1,000-1,500 eggs.
habitat: Occurs near virtually any freshwater habitat and in some places slightly brackish marshes.
Breeds in still, shallow, permanent or temporary water.
range: Lowlands of the southeastern United States from southern New York to the Florida Keys, west to eastern Kansas, central Oklahoma and eastern Texas; introduced on Little Bahama Bank. Not reported for Canada in the source.
